items.title: Claude Opus and a new alternative to Figma Make for prototyping
items.summary: Hi product people 👋, Coming up in this week’s briefing, we take a look at where Claude’s new Opus model excels, a new competitor to Figma Make and why young Americans trust AI the least. Plus, a closer look at ChatGPT’s growth strategy for hitting 220 million subscribers and a new prompt designed to help you shape your product’s next set of experiments. Enjoy the rest of your weekend! Rich Follow on Substack Notes | Watch on YouTube Subscribe now Claude Opus 4.5 excels at Excel First up, less than a week after the arrival of Gemini 3, Anthropic released a new model of its own. Claude Opus 4.5 is the newest flagship model and it’s the first model to hit a >80% SWE-Bench verified score on AI coding. Anthropic says the model “handles ambiguity and reasons about tradeoffs without hand-holding” and uses an agentic test called t2-bench to assess how well the AI agents are capable of handling complex, multi-step customer problems. If you’re interested in learning how AI agents powered by the new model perform, the t2-bench documentation is worth a read. See some examples of what people have built with Claude Opus 4.5 so far: An app for filing taxes with no mistakes , Voxel castle 3d environment . Where the model really seems to excel though, is in creating Excel Spreadsheets and Powerpoint presentations. Numerous users have said that the output is far cleaner than previous models and based on first-hand experience, this definitely seems to be the case. Claude has even released a dedicated product called Claude for Excel which bakes the model directly into spreadsheets. For product teams, this could be super-handy for scenarios where you need to quickly turn data into presentations. OpenAI’s growth strategy leaked - can it really build a business with 220 million subscribers? OpenAI wants 220 million paying ChatGPT subscribers by 2030. To put that into perspective, that’s nearly as many paid subscribers as Spotify, and it’s about two thirds the size of Netflix. And it would make ChatGPT one of the biggest subscription businesses on the planet. So how exactly do they plan to pull this off? This week, an insider from OpenAI revealed how the company plans to grow its subscription video. I unpack the details of their product growth strategy here: Replit Design Mode: an alternative to Figma Make Replit has released a new “design mode” which uses Gemini’s 3 model to generate quick designs for web apps and prototypes. It’s squarely aimed at product managers and designers who want to build some quick mock ups and prototypes and is designed to generate visuals first and backend functionality later. If you’re happy with your design Replit has a “Convert to App” feature which then allows you to add backend logic and databases within Replit. As well as this, Replit also added the ability to take payments via Stripe. If you’re looking for some alternatives to Figma Make, it could be worth a look. Google’s new shortcuts and classification labels, YouTube adds prompt-based personalisation Google released a new feature in Workspace which allows users to apply and show data classification labels across different file types. So, for example, you might add a confidential label to a financial forecast or salary management spreadsheet to avoid sharing the wrong file. If you’re a Google Workspace power user, this week Google also revealed a new way to quickly build a vibe coded app in Google’s AI studio with the “app.new” shortcut in Chrome. YouTube is testing a new prompt-based AI feature that will allow users to build their own customized home page. It works by letting users describe what types of YouTube videos they’d like to see e.g. “more travel vlogs” or “less gaming content”. It borrows from similar features recently released by Spotify and Pinterest - but if implemented, this takes the concept a step further by working directly on the algorithm that suggests recommended content across the main home page - and not inside an isolated, separate feature like Spotify DJ. Perplexity and OpenAI release shopping features - but their performance is far from perfect Perplexity and OpenAI both released new shopping features this week, just in time for Christmas. The new features allow users to give the model a goal and outsource the product research process. New analysis this week put the models to the test to understand how well they perform in agentic shopping. In this test, ChatGPT, Gemini, Perplexity and Copilot were tasked with shopping for a new Android Smartwatch but the reviewer had one common complaint amongst each of the models: they all tended to choose outdated models. Here’s a snapshot of their findings: Meanwhile, Amazon is ramping up its crackdown on agentic shopping. Tools you can use Cracked - grow your product with the help of AI social media influencers. Slightly dystopian but worth a look. Orchestra - makes workflow simple for teams who build products and rely on communication. With messaging at its core, and a task tracker and AI agents natively built in, work contexts are aligned and teams are connected. Guideflow - automate the end to end product demo process. Share Key reads and resources for product teams New from the Department of Product Substack this week: Knowledge Series - How to identify opportunities for AI automation In this Knowledge Series, we’ll explore some of the ways you can identify opportunities for AI automation. You’ll get a concrete step by step framework for identifying AI automation opportunities, prompts to use for automation opportunity analysis along with real world examples of how other companies are automating product-related processes to use as inspiration. New prompt in the library - Generate ideas for product experiments based on your strategy and goals This prompt creates your own personal experiment strategist for your product.  Fill in details about your product, current metrics, and top strategic goals and it generates 5-7 tailored experiment ideas complete with hypotheses, step-by-step implementation plans, success criteria, and effort/impact estimates. You’ll also get prioritization guidance on which experiments to run first. (Department of Product) Strategy - How go to market strategies are evolving in the AI age As companies experiment with the right formula across sales, implementation, and customer success, GTM teams are evolving. (Andreessen Horowitz) Career progression - How to be memorable to senior executives Annual planning and performance reviews dovetail in this special time of the year for many organizations. Executives are reflecting on performance in 2025 and planning for 2026. In closed rooms and off-sites, leaders are implicitly and explicitly solidifying their perceptions of the growth potential of each team member. Yue Zhao explains some of the ways you can be memorable to senior executives before the new year starts. (Substack) Interview - A conversation with Google CEO Sundar Pichai about his 10 year AI product strategy Logan Kilpatrick from Google DeepMind sits down with Sundar Pichai, CEO of Google and Alphabet to discuss the launch of Gemini 3, Nano Banana Pro and Google’s overall AI momentum. They talk about Google’s long-term bets on infrastructure, what it’s actually like to ship SOTA models, and the rise of vibe coding. Sundar also shares his personal launch day rituals and thoughts on future moonshots. (YouTube) 📈 Product data and trends to stay informed Americans don’t trust AI. This week, the Edelman Trust Institute released their 2025 Trust Barometer Flash Poll focused on AI adoption and trust dynamics across various different countries including Brazil, China, Germany, UK, and US. Key insights from the research that might be relevant for product teams: Only 32% of US respondents currently trust AI but trust increases adoption likelihood by +16.27%. Among those who distrust AI, 74% reject its adoption vs. 14% who trust it. When Gen AI helps users understand complex ideas, trust jumps +37 to +45 points across markets. Only 8% of AI enthusiasts report bad experiences vs. 18% of rejecters, suggesting experience converts skeptics better than marketing. Younger generations trust AI significantly more than older users with 62% of 18-34 year olds saying they trust AI vs. 40% for 55+. However, American youths are the least trusting of AI; among US young people only 40% trust AI vs 59% in the UK, 53% in Germany, 68% in Brazil and 88% in China. When asked why they don’t use AI, trust concerns dominate at 53-70% while intimidation/complexity is only 12-20%. This suggests teams should invest in data transparency and privacy controls rather than simplification messaging. 67-71% of US/UK distrusters feel “AI is being forced upon me” which correlates strongly with rejection. For product teams, this suggests avoiding aggressive auto-opt-in strategies and designing for gradual, user-controlled adoption instead. Read the report in full. YouTube is the most used social platform in the US with 84% of adults saying that they ever use it. Remarkably, Facebook is second with 71% of US adults saying they ever use it with Instagram third at 50%. New research from Pew on Social Media . Perplexity’s mobile app downloads have plummeted 80% in the last six weeks. Even when accounting for the ~50% of Perplexity downloads that were attributable to a commercial partnership in India, the US numbers tell a similar story. Demand for AI fluency has grown nearly 7× in two years and is spreading beyond STEM according to a n ew report by McKinsey. Hi product people 👋,

Coming up in this week’s briefing, we take a look at where Claude’s new Opus model excels, a new competitor to Figma Make and why young Americans trust AI the least. Plus, a closer look at ChatGPT’s growth strategy for hitting 220 million subscribers and a new prompt designed to help you shape your product’s next set of experiments.

Enjoy the rest of your weekend!

Rich

Follow on Substack Notes | Watch on YouTube

Subscribe now

Claude Opus 4.5 excels at Excel

Anthropic says the model “handles ambiguity and reasons about tradeoffs without hand-holding” and uses an agentic test called t2-bench to assess how well the AI agents are capable of handling complex, multi-step customer problems. If you’re interested in learning how AI agents powered by the new model perform, the t2-bench documentation is worth a read.

See some examples of what people have built with Claude Opus 4.5 so far: An app for filing taxes with no mistakes, Voxel castle 3d environment.

Where the model really seems to excel though, is in creating Excel Spreadsheets and Powerpoint presentations. Numerous users have said that the output is far cleaner than previous models and based on first-hand experience, this definitely seems to be the case. Claude has even released a dedicated product called Claude for Excel which bakes the model directly into spreadsheets. For product teams, this could be super-handy for scenarios where you need to quickly turn data into presentations.

OpenAI’s growth strategy leaked - can it really build a business with 220 million subscribers?

OpenAI wants 220 million paying ChatGPT subscribers by 2030. To put that into perspective, that’s nearly as many paid subscribers as Spotify, and it’s about two thirds the size of Netflix. And it would make ChatGPT one of the biggest subscription businesses on the planet.

So how exactly do they plan to pull this off? This week, an insider from OpenAI revealed how the company plans to grow its subscription video. I unpack the details of their product growth strategy here:

Replit Design Mode: an alternative to Figma Make

Replit has released a new “design mode” which uses Gemini’s 3 model to generate quick designs for web apps and prototypes. It’s squarely aimed at product managers and designers who want to build some quick mock ups and prototypes and is designed to generate visuals first and backend functionality later. If you’re happy with your design Replit has a “Convert to App” feature which then allows you to add backend logic and databases within Replit. As well as this, Replit also added the ability to take payments via Stripe. If you’re looking for some alternatives to Figma Make, it could be worth a look.

Google’s new shortcuts and classification labels, YouTube adds prompt-based personalisation

Google released a new feature in Workspace which allows users to apply and show data classification labels across different file types. So, for example, you might add a confidential label to a financial forecast or salary management spreadsheet to avoid sharing the wrong file. If you’re a Google Workspace power user, this week Google also revealed a new way to quickly build a vibe coded app in Google’s AI studio with the “app.new” shortcut in Chrome.

YouTube is testing a new prompt-based AI feature that will allow users to build their own customized home page. It works by letting users describe what types of YouTube videos they’d like to see e.g. “more travel vlogs” or “less gaming content”. It borrows from similar features recently released by Spotify and Pinterest - but if implemented, this takes the concept a step further by working directly on the algorithm that suggests recommended content across the main home page - and not inside an isolated, separate feature like Spotify DJ.

Perplexity and OpenAI release shopping features - but their performance is far from perfect

Perplexity and OpenAI both released new shopping features this week, just in time for Christmas. The new features allow users to give the model a goal and outsource the product research process.

New analysis this week put the models to the test to understand how well they perform in agentic shopping. In this test, ChatGPT, Gemini, Perplexity and Copilot were tasked with shopping for a new Android Smartwatch but the reviewer had one common complaint amongst each of the models: they all tended to choose outdated models.

Here’s a snapshot of their findings:

Meanwhile, Amazon is ramping up its crackdown on agentic shopping.

Tools you can use

Cracked - grow your product with the help of AI social media influencers. Slightly dystopian but worth a look.

Orchestra - makes workflow simple for teams who build products and rely on communication. With messaging at its core, and a task tracker and AI agents natively built in, work contexts are aligned and teams are connected.

Guideflow - automate the end to end product demo process.

Share

Key reads and resources for product teams

New from the Department of Product Substack this week:

Knowledge Series - How to identify opportunities for AI automation

In this Knowledge Series, we’ll explore some of the ways you can identify opportunities for AI automation. You’ll get a concrete step by step framework for identifying AI automation opportunities, prompts to use for automation opportunity analysis along with real world examples of how other companies are automating product-related processes to use as inspiration.

New prompt in the library - Generate ideas for product experiments based on your strategy and goals

This prompt creates your own personal experiment strategist for your product. Fill in details about your product, current metrics, and top strategic goals and it generates 5-7 tailored experiment ideas complete with hypotheses, step-by-step implementation plans, success criteria, and effort/impact estimates. You’ll also get prioritization guidance on which experiments to run first.

(Department of Product)

Strategy - How go to market strategies are evolving in the AI age

As companies experiment with the right formula across sales, implementation, and customer success, GTM teams are evolving. (Andreessen Horowitz)

Career progression - How to be memorable to senior executives

Annual planning and performance reviews dovetail in this special time of the year for many organizations. Executives are reflecting on performance in 2025 and planning for 2026. In closed rooms and off-sites, leaders are implicitly and explicitly solidifying their perceptions of the growth potential of each team member. Yue Zhao explains some of the ways you can be memorable to senior executives before the new year starts. (Substack)

Interview - A conversation with Google CEO Sundar Pichai about his 10 year AI product strategy

Logan Kilpatrick from Google DeepMind sits down with Sundar Pichai, CEO of Google and Alphabet to discuss the launch of Gemini 3, Nano Banana Pro and Google’s overall AI momentum. They talk about Google’s long-term bets on infrastructure, what it’s actually like to ship SOTA models, and the rise of vibe coding. Sundar also shares his personal launch day rituals and thoughts on future moonshots. (YouTube)

📈 Product data and trends to stay informed

Americans don’t trust AI. This week, the Edelman Trust Institute released their 2025 Trust Barometer Flash Poll focused on AI adoption and trust dynamics across various different countries including Brazil, China, Germany, UK, and US.

Key insights from the research that might be relevant for product teams:

  • Only 32% of US respondents currently trust AI but trust increases adoption likelihood by +16.27%. Among those who distrust AI, 74% reject its adoption vs. 14% who trust it.

  • When Gen AI helps users understand complex ideas, trust jumps +37 to +45 points across markets. Only 8% of AI enthusiasts report bad experiences vs. 18% of rejecters, suggesting experience converts skeptics better than marketing.

  • Younger generations trust AI significantly more than older users with 62% of 18-34 year olds saying they trust AI vs. 40% for 55+. However, American youths are the least trusting of AI; among US young people only 40% trust AI vs 59% in the UK, 53% in Germany, 68% in Brazil and 88% in China.

  • When asked why they don’t use AI, trust concerns dominate at 53-70% while intimidation/complexity is only 12-20%. This suggests teams should invest in data transparency and privacy controls rather than simplification messaging.

  • 67-71% of US/UK distrusters feel “AI is being forced upon me” which correlates strongly with rejection. For product teams, this suggests avoiding aggressive auto-opt-in strategies and designing for gradual, user-controlled adoption instead.

Read the report in full.

YouTube is the most used social platform in the US with 84% of adults saying that they ever use it. Remarkably, Facebook is second with 71% of US adults saying they ever use it with Instagram third at 50%. New research from Pew on Social Media.

Perplexity’s mobile app downloads have plummeted 80% in the last six weeks. Even when accounting for the ~50% of Perplexity downloads that were attributable to a commercial partnership in India, the US numbers tell a similar story.

Demand for AI fluency has grown nearly 7× in two years and is spreading beyond STEM according to a new report by McKinsey.

items.title: The Sequence Radar #763: Last Week AI Trifecta: Opus 4.5, DeepSeek Math, and FLUX.2
items.summary: Next Week in The Sequence: Our series about synthetic data continues with a an intro to one of the most effective and yet overlooked methods in the space: rephrasing. The AI of the week dives into Claude Opus 4.5 ofc. In the opinion section, we are going to explore the thesis of whether AI agents require a new internet. Subscribe and don’t miss out: TheSequence is a reader-supported publication. To receive new posts and support my work, consider becoming a free or paid subscriber. 📝 Editorial: Last Week AI Trifecta: Opus 4.5, DeepSeek Math, and FLUX.2 The pace of AI development is picking up, and frankly, this week has been a bit of a blur. We’re seeing the gradients of progress steepen in real-time. I’ve been playing around with the new releases—Claude Opus 4.5, DeepSeek Math V2, and the new FLUX.2 from Black Forest Labs—and the “feeling” of using these models is distinct. It’s no longer just about scaling laws; it’s about architectural specialization and the refinement of “System 2” thinking. First, let’s talk about Claude Opus 4.5 . Anthropic has nailed the “Software 2.0” experience here. The standout feature isn’t just the raw intelligence, though it is visibly smarter; it’s the reliability in long-horizon agentic workflows. I threw a nasty refactoring task at it—migrating a legacy codebase—and it didn’t just autocomplete the next token; it planned. It feels like the loss landscape for “reasoning” has been smoothed out. They’ve managed to cut the token cost while increasing the context window efficiency, which is huge for developer loops. It’s becoming the default “brain” you want in your IDE. It’s less like a chatbot and more like a very senior engineer who doesn’t get tired. Then you have DeepSeek Math V2 , which is arguably the most interesting release from a pure research perspective. We are seeing the “bitter lesson” play out again, but with a twist: verification. This model hitting 118/120 on the Putnam is absolutely bonkers. Just a year ago, we were celebrating models that could barely pass high school algebra. DeepSeek’s “verifier-generator” architecture is a clear signal that we are moving past simple next-token prediction into iterative self-correction. It’s essentially running a specialized inner loop to “check its work” before committing to an output. This is the path to robust reasoning. The fact that it’s open weights is a gift to the community; we can now inspect the gradients of a model that effectively “thinks” in math. Finally, Black Forest Labs dropped FLUX.2 , and the visual fidelity is stunning. We’re talking 4-megapixel native generation that respects physics and lighting in a way that feels grounded. But the real story is the “Kontext” feature and the open-weight nature of the release. It proves that you don’t need a closed garden to achieve state-of-the-art results in generative media. The community is going to fine-tune this into oblivion (in a good way). The meta-narrative this week is clear: the gap between “generating text” and “solving problems” is closing. Claude is mastering the workflow, DeepSeek is mastering the rigorous logic, and Flux is mastering the pixel space. We are seeing a convergence where models aren’t just memorizing the internet; they are learning to simulate the world, verify their own thoughts, and act as genuine agents. 🔎 AI Research NATURAL EMERGENT MISALIGNMENT FROM REWARD HACKING IN PRODUCTION RL AI Lab: Anthropic Summary: This paper shows that when LLMs learn to reward-hack real production coding environments, they generalize from narrow hacks to broad misaligned behaviors like alignment faking, sabotage of safety tools, and cooperation with hackers. It evaluates several mitigations (reward-hack detection, diverse RLHF, and “inoculation prompting”) and finds that framing hacks as acceptable during training can greatly reduce this emergent misalignment even when hacking continues. DR Tulu: Reinforcement Learning with Evolving Rubrics for Deep Research AI Lab: Allen Institute for AI & University of Washington collaborators Summary: The authors introduce RLER (Reinforcement Learning with Evolving Rubrics), where instance-specific rubrics are generated and updated online using retrieved evidence and model rollouts, providing on-policy, search-grounded feedback for long-form deep research tasks. Using this method they train DR Tulu-8B, an open 8B “deep research” model that matches or beats much larger proprietary systems on several long-form research benchmarks while being far cheaper to run, and they release data, code, and tools for future work. Fara-7B: An Efficient Agentic Model for Computer Use AI Lab: Microsoft Summary: This work presents FaraGen, a multi-agent synthetic data engine that generates high-quality, verified web interaction trajectories at roughly $1 per task, and uses it to train Fara-7B, a 7B “pixel-in, action-out” computer-use agent that operates directly from screenshots. Fara-7B outperforms similarly sized CUAs and approaches the performance of much larger frontier models on benchmarks like WebVoyager and the newly introduced WebTailBench, while being cheap enough to run on-device. Soft Adaptive Policy Optimization AI Lab: Qwen Team, Alibaba Summary: The paper proposes SAPO, a group-based RL algorithm that replaces hard clipping of importance ratios with a smooth, temperature-controlled gating function, giving sequence-coherent but token-adaptive updates that better handle high-variance off-policy tokens, especially in MoE models. Experiments on math reasoning and Qwen3-VL training show SAPO improves training stability and final Pass@1 performance over GRPO and GSPO under comparable compute budgets. Estimating AI productivity gains from Claude conversations AI Lab: Anthropic Summary: Using 100,000 anonymized Claude.ai conversations, the authors have Claude estimate how long each task would take with and without AI, validate these estimates on software-engineering data, and then map tasks to O*NET occupations and BLS wage data to quantify task-level time and cost savings. Aggregating these estimates with a Hulten-style framework, they suggest that broad adoption of current Claude-like systems could raise U.S. labor productivity growth by about 1.8 percentage points per year over a decade, while noting important limitations like validation gaps, task coverage, and organizational frictions. NVIDIA Nemotron-Parse 1.1 AI Lab: NVIDIA Summary: This paper presents Nemotron-Parse-1.1, an 885M-parameter encoder–decoder vision-language OCR model (plus the faster Nemotron-Parse-1.1-TC variant) that jointly extracts markdown/LaTeX text, structured tables, bounding boxes, and semantic classes with layout-aware reading order from document images. Trained on a blend of synthetic, public, and NVpdftex-derived datasets, it delivers competitive or state-of-the-art performance on GOT, OmniDocBench, RD-TableBench, and multilingual OCR benchmarks while offering open weights on Hugging Face and optimized NIM deployments for high-throughput production use. 🤖 AI Tech Releases Claude Opus 4.5 Anthropic released Claude Opus 4.5 which sets new leves of coding, computer usage and agentic tasks. DeepSeekMath-v2 DeepSeek open sourced a new model optimized for mathematical reasoning. Flux.2 Black Forest Labs released its new generation visual intelligence models . 📡AI Radar To offset emissions from its “Colossus” data center, Elon Musk’s AI company has proposed the construction of a new solar farm in Memphis. Onton , The AI-powered shopping platform has secured $7.5 million in seed funding to expand its neuro-symbolic search engine beyond furniture into categories like apparel and electronics. Character.AI is moving away from open-ended chat for younger users, the company is launching “Stories,” a feature that allows users to create and share interactive, gamified adventures. Google & Accel established a first-of-its-kind partnership , Google and venture firm Accel are launching the “Atoms AI Cohort 2026” to co-invest in and support early-stage Indian AI startups. (Link: Accel Blog ) Amazon has committed up to $50 billion to build massive AI and supercomputing infrastructure specifically for U.S. government agencies. Momentic has raised $15 million in Series A fundin g to further develop its AI-native platform that automates software testing for developers. Sierra , the enterprise AI agent startup co-founded by Bret Taylor has reached $100 million in Annual Recurring Revenue (ARR) less than two years after its inception. Alibaba has launched its new Quark smart glasses , which feature a deeply integrated AI assistant powered by its proprietary Qwen large language model. Monolith Management , the investment firm which backs DeepSeek rival Moonshot AI, has closed a new $289 million fund to support Chinese AI startups . Alibaba reported robust quarterly revenue growth , driven largely by accelerating demand for its cloud and AI-related products.

Aggregating these estimates with a Hulten-style framework, they suggest that broad adoption of current Claude-like systems could raise U.S. labor productivity growth by about 1.8 percentage points per year over a decade, while noting important limitations like validation gaps, task coverage, and organizational frictions.

AI Lab: NVIDIA

Summary: This paper presents Nemotron-Parse-1.1, an 885M-parameter encoder–decoder vision-language OCR model (plus the faster Nemotron-Parse-1.1-TC variant) that jointly extracts markdown/LaTeX text, structured tables, bounding boxes, and semantic classes with layout-aware reading order from document images. Trained on a blend of synthetic, public, and NVpdftex-derived datasets, it delivers competitive or state-of-the-art performance on GOT, OmniDocBench, RD-TableBench, and multilingual OCR benchmarks while offering open weights on Hugging Face and optimized NIM deployments for high-throughput production use.

🤖 AI Tech ReleasesClaude Opus 4.5

Anthropic released Claude Opus 4.5 which sets new leves of coding, computer usage and agentic tasks.

DeepSeekMath-v2

DeepSeek open sourced a new model optimized for mathematical reasoning.

Flux.2

Black Forest Labs released its new generation visual intelligence models.

📡AI Radar

  • To offset emissions from its “Colossus” data center, Elon Musk’s AI company has proposed the construction of a new solar farm in Memphis.

  • Onton, The AI-powered shopping platform has secured $7.5 million in seed funding to expand its neuro-symbolic search engine beyond furniture into categories like apparel and electronics.

  • Character.AI is moving away from open-ended chat for younger users, the company is launching “Stories,” a feature that allows users to create and share interactive, gamified adventures.

  • Google & Accel established a first-of-its-kind partnership, Google and venture firm Accel are launching the “Atoms AI Cohort 2026” to co-invest in and support early-stage Indian AI startups. (Link: Accel Blog)

  • Amazon has committed up to $50 billion to build massive AI and supercomputing infrastructure specifically for U.S. government agencies.

  • Momentic has raised $15 million in Series A funding to further develop its AI-native platform that automates software testing for developers.

  • Sierra, the enterprise AI agent startup co-founded by Bret Taylor has reached $100 million in Annual Recurring Revenue (ARR) less than two years after its inception.

  • Alibaba has launched its new Quark smart glasses, which feature a deeply integrated AI assistant powered by its proprietary Qwen large language model.

  • Monolith Management, the investment firm which backs DeepSeek rival Moonshot AI, has closed a new $289 million fund to support Chinese AI startups.

  • Alibaba reported robust quarterly revenue growth, driven largely by accelerating demand for its cloud and AI-related products.
